nodes.title: Quadratic unit action in additive coordinates
nodes.statement: For s in Z/2, define τ_s on the existing additive group Z × Z/2 by τ_s(a,b)=(-a,b+s·(a mod 2)). This is the action of the nonidentity element of C₂; τ_s is additive and τ_s²=id.
hypotheses: No field or chosen fundamental unit is part of this definition.
proofSteps: Use the ordinary integer-to-ZMod cast for a mod 2.
Additivity follows from distributivity and cast additivity. Applying τ_s twice cancels the two shear terms.
Its values on (1,0) and (0,1) determine the action and its parameter.

nodes.title: A square-killed kernel is detected on the two-primary subgroup
nodes.statement: Let q:G→H be a surjective homomorphism of commutative groups, and assume x²=1 for every x in ker q. Then q is bijective iff its restriction is bijective from G[2∞] to H[2∞], using the canonical subgroups CommGroup.primaryComponent. No finiteness assumption is required.
hypotheses: G,H commutative groups; q surjective; its kernel killed by two.
proofSteps: Every homomorphism preserves membership in the canonical primary subgroup by mapping the annihilating power.
If q is bijective and y^(2^k)=1, its unique preimage x has q(x^(2^k))=1; injectivity gives x^(2^k)=1, proving surjectivity of the restriction.
Conversely every kernel element is in G[2∞], with exponent witness k=1. Injectivity of the restricted map compares that element to one and makes the whole kernel trivial.
A homomorphism with trivial kernel is injective; combine with the assumed surjectivity.

nodes.title: Negative Pell and norm-minus-one units for every squarefree radicand
nodes.statement: Under the quadratic presentation hypotheses, there exist integers x,y with x²-dy²=-1 iff there is a unit u of the full ring O_K with N_K/Q(u)=-1. This interface removes the mod-four condition by joining the two existing parent targets.
hypotheses: d>1 is a squarefree integer; K is a number field with θ in O_K.
minpoly_Z(θ)=X²-d and Q[θ]=K; these hypotheses specify the quadratic presentation.
proofSteps: Use the parent order-to-unit embedding for the forward implication.
If d is not 1 modulo 4, O_K=Z[θ], and read the inverse coordinates and norm from the parent comparison.
If d is 1 modulo 4, invoke the reviewed half-coordinate parent target: d=1 modulo 8 puts any unit in Z[θ]; d=5 modulo 8 puts its cube there. The odd power preserves norm minus one.
The condition d>1 excludes the degree-one radicand, where quadratic norm transport would be false.

nodes.title: Negative Pell and the narrow principal square-root class
nodes.statement: Under the quadratic presentation hypotheses, x²-dy²=-1 has an integral solution iff mkPrincipal(θ)=1 in Cl⁺(K). Here θ is read as a unit of the field K, not as an integral unit; θ≠0 follows from its minimal polynomial.
hypotheses: d>1 is a squarefree integer; K is a number field with θ in O_K.
minpoly_Z(θ)=X²-d and Q[θ]=K; these hypotheses specify the quadratic presentation.
proofSteps: The parent norm bridge turns Pell solubility into an integral unit of norm -1. Since N(θ)=-d, N(θu)=d>0. The pinned quadratic sign lemma makes θu or -θu totally positive, and the pinned mkPrincipal criterion proves triviality.

Conversely mkPrincipal(θ)=1 supplies a unit w with wθ totally positive. The two real embeddings send θ to opposite roots of d; therefore w has opposite signs at these embeddings. Its norm is negative and, being an integral unit norm, equals -1.
Return through the all-radicand comparison. Changing θ to -θ does not change its principal ideal or the result.

nodes.statement: Under the quadratic presentation hypotheses, x²-dy²=-1 has an integral solution iff the natural map q:Cl⁺(K)→Cl(K) restricts bijectively from Cl⁺(K)[2∞] to Cl(K)[2∞]. This is a statement about q, not merely about abstract isomorphism types.
hypotheses: d>1 is a squarefree integer; K is a number field with θ in O_K.
minpoly_Z(θ)=X²-d and Q[θ]=K; these hypotheses specify the quadratic presentation.
proofSteps: The pinned quadratic narrow-class theorem identifies injectivity of q with existence of a norm-minus-one unit; combine it with the parent order bridge.
The pinned forgetful map is surjective and its kernel is killed by two. Apply two-primary-detects-bijectivity.
The squarefree and d>1 hypotheses enter the order bridge; the group-theoretic detection step itself uses neither number fields nor finiteness.

nodes.title: The Galois action on the full quadratic unit group
nodes.statement: Under the quadratic presentation hypotheses, there exist s in Z/2 and an additive equivalence F:Additive(O_Kˣ)→Z×Z/2 with F(-1)=(0,1), F(σu)=τ_s(F(u)) for every unit u, and s=1 iff negative Pell is integrally soluble. Here σ is the pinned ring-of-integers quadratic conjugation. Consequently the soluble case has the Galois module in Koymans–Pagano item 9, while the insoluble case has τ_0. Equivalently, negative Pell is soluble iff an additive equivalence carrying -1 to (0,1) intertwines conjugation with τ_1.
hypotheses: d>1 is a squarefree integer; K is a number field with θ in O_K.
minpoly_Z(θ)=X²-d and Q[θ]=K; these hypotheses specify the quadratic presentation.
proofSteps: The real quadratic presentation gives two real places, no complex places, and unit rank one. Evaluate a torsion unit at a real embedding: a real root of unity is ±1, and the embedding is injective; hence the torsion is exactly {±1}.
Apply the pinned Dirichlet product equivalence, reindex its single free coordinate and identify the torsion coordinate with Z/2. This gives a generator ε and unique expressions ε^a(-1)^b.
The pinned norm identity yields εσε=(-1)^s for exactly one s. Thus σε=ε^(-1)(-1)^s, while σ(-1)=-1; multiplying these formulas gives τ_s on all coordinates.
Since N(-1)=1 in degree two, a norm-minus-one unit exists exactly when s=1. Use the all-radicand negative Pell comparison.

For the converse characterization by τ_1, take the inverse image of (1,0). Its sum with its conjugate is the inverse image of (0,1), namely -1. The conjugation norm formula then gives a unit of norm -1, and the order bridge gives negative Pell. Thus an abstract action comparison is not inferred merely from one choice of normal form.
Changing ε to its inverse or to -ε leaves its norm sign unchanged; the coordinate equivalence is existential and requires no canonical choice.

For d=3, ε=2+θ has norm +1 and the parameter is zero.

The torsion coordinate is fixed for every d.

nodes.title: A rigorous determinant enclosure from entrywise errors
nodes.statement: Let E,Ê be real r×r matrices and B,δ nonnegative reals. If |E_ij|≤B and |Ê_ij-E_ij|≤δ for every i,j, then |det Ê-det E|≤r!·r·δ·(B+δ)^(r-1), with natural subtraction in the exponent. The same bound controls ||det Ê|-|det E||. At r=0 both determinants are one and the error is zero.
hypotheses: Uniform bound is on the exact entries E, not only on approximate entries; δ and B nonnegative.
proofSteps: Bound every approximate entry by B+δ using the triangle inequality.
For r≥1 and each permutation, telescope the difference of the two products into r terms. Each contains one entry difference bounded by δ and r-1 entries bounded by B+δ.
Use the Leibniz determinant formula, the triangle inequality and the r! permutations to sum these bounds.
For r=0 use Matrix.det_isEmpty separately. Apply the reverse triangle inequality to the absolute determinants.
For a log table use weights 1 at real places and 2 at complex places before applying the bound; errors must refer to the weighted entries.

nodes.title: Class-number and regulator certification from rigorous intervals
nodes.statement: Let φ:Z^N→Additive Cl(K) be surjective; let A be a square integer matrix with nonzero determinant and φ(A_col_j)=0 for all j. Let u be a unit family of size rank K satisfying IsMaxRank. Write h=classNumber K, R=regulator K and R_u=regOfFamily u. Suppose ε,η≥0, |Rhat-R_u|≤ε, |a-hR|≤η, and |det A|·(Rhat+ε)<2(a-η). Then range A=ker φ, the subgroup generated by u and torsion is all units, |det A|=h, and R_u=R. No GRH assumption occurs in this soundness theorem; a producer must justify the stated intervals.
hypotheses: φ surjective; nonzero determinant; every column is a genuine relation.
Maximal-rank units; rigorously valid error intervals; strict inequality.
proofSteps: The parent determinant contract gives |det A|=h·i, where i=[ker φ:range A] is a positive integer.
Pinned regulator positivity and regOfFamily_div_regulator give R_u=R·j, where j is the positive index of the subgroup generated by units and torsion.
The interval hypotheses imply R_u≤Rhat+ε and a-η≤hR. Hence hR·ij=|det A|R_u<2hR. Positivity of hR implies ij<2.
Positive integers i,j therefore both equal one. Apply relative-index-one and index-one to obtain completeness, and substitute back for the numerical equalities.
determinant-entrywise-enclosure supplies ε when Rhat is an absolute determinant of a rigorous weighted log table. An analytic or enumerative producer supplies η independently.

sources.match: The paper certifies tentative class number and regulator through rigorous approximations and an index bound below two. The entrywise error estimate and two-sided interval interface below are explicit local refinements, not a quotation of its numerical constants or an analytic bound producer.

acceptance: Exact intervals ε=η=0 recover the parent joint certificate.
An index-two relation lattice or an index-two unit family makes the left product at least 2hR and cannot pass.
Equality at the threshold two is rejected; rounding below two without a rigorous ε is rejected.
Rank zero uses the empty determinant one and the torsion subgroup as the full unit group; N=0 is allowed only when φ is surjective onto the trivial class group.

coverage.note: Closed mathematical planning in this follow-up, using the accepted parent targets and the resolution ledger. All Lean theorem proofs remain admitted and all implementation statuses unchecked. Koymans–Pagano route 7 has no positional acceptance verdict; this external queue boundary is recorded separately and no source-route approval is asserted.

frontierResolution.disposition: Planning obligation supplied; not an implementation claim.
frontierResolution.resolution: Use the finite product of powers of ideal classes as the homomorphism; its additive kernel is a Z-submodule. The image equals the generated subgroup, and the quotient-kernel equivalence plus finiteness gives index h. The nonnegative-principality API refers to ideal classes, not ideal equality.

frontierResolution.disposition: Planning obligation supplied; not an implementation claim.
frontierResolution.resolution: Import CA.3/cokernel-of-an-integer-matrix. If the Smith rank were below the row count, projection onto one free Z coordinate would give a surjection from the finite class group to infinite Z, a contradiction. Thus there is no free factor; the complete relation lattice is essential.

frontierResolution.disposition: Planning obligation supplied; not an implementation claim.
frontierResolution.resolution: Nonzero det gives a full-rank column lattice of index |det A| by AddSubgroup.index_eq_natAbs_det. Index multiplication with the kernel of a surjective presentation gives |det A|=h·i. Since this index is nonzero, i is positive; relative-index-one gives determinant equality iff completeness.

frontierResolution.disposition: Planning obligation supplied; not an implementation claim.
frontierResolution.resolution: The relation and unit indices are positive; the product is hR·ij. A certified h*≤hR and a strict product below 2h* force ij=1. Both group equalities and both numerical equalities follow. The interval refinement records the error budget explicitly.

frontierResolution.disposition: Planning obligation supplied; not an implementation claim.
frontierResolution.resolution: For 0≠a in I, multiplication by a embeds O_K in I. Its rational extension is invertible, so I has full rank; alternatively the integral characteristic polynomial gives a nonzero integer in (a)⊆I. Apply the imported CA.3 Hermite existence and uniqueness to any integral basis of I, obtaining a square H and equality of the column lattice with I.

frontierResolution.disposition: Planning obligation supplied; not an implementation claim.
frontierResolution.resolution: Transport the column basis through the integral basis equivalence, then apply Ideal.natAbs_det_basis_change. Positive triangular pivots make |det H| equal their product; the top and integer principal-ideal cases check the dimension power.

frontierResolution.disposition: Planning obligation supplied; not an implementation claim.
frontierResolution.resolution: Use the existing Algebra.leftMulMatrix, not an undefined multiplier. Stable columns give integer coefficients X_k with M_kH=HX_k. Conversely these equations preserve the lattice under multiplication by every basis element; linearity preserves it under all of O_K, defining a unique ideal. Nonzero det makes it nonzero. The suggested endpoint states this without an HNF carrier.

frontierResolution.disposition: Planning obligation supplied; not an implementation claim.
frontierResolution.resolution: Read integer coordinates C in an existing integral basis. The change-of-family formula gives discr b=(det C)^2d_K even for dependent b. Since d_K≠0, discr equality is equivalent to det C=±1, and the adjugate gives an integral inverse and a basis. If discr b is squarefree it is nonzero and a nonunit det would introduce a prime square divisor. Finite-index transport uses the range basis and the pinned determinant-cardinality theorem.

frontierResolution.disposition: Planning obligation supplied; not an implementation claim.
frontierResolution.resolution: Monogenicity discharges exponent θ=1 by RingOfIntegers.exponent_eq_one_iff, hence p does not divide that exponent for any prime p. Apply the existing primesOverSpanEquivMonicFactorsMod, its span formula, inertia degree and multiplicity ramification theorems. Do not exclude primes dividing the field discriminant.

frontierResolution.disposition: Planning obligation supplied; not an implementation claim.
frontierResolution.resolution: Use Zsqrtd.lift at θ²=d. Its value is x+yθ and its image is the integral adjoin. A vanishing image would give a rational square root unless both coefficients vanish. The quadratic integral-basis result determines surjectivity; norm_add_mul_gen proves norm transport. The degree-one counterexample is excluded.

frontierResolution.disposition: Planning obligation supplied; not an implementation claim.
frontierResolution.resolution: In the maximal order case, use the order isomorphism and Zsqrtd norm-unitary comparison. The unit norm lands in {±1}, so its kernel has index one or two by the quotient-kernel equivalence. Pell.IsFundamental.eq_zpow_or_neg_zpow supplies generation up to sign. This norm-one generator need not generate every full-ring unit.

frontierResolution.disposition: Planning obligation supplied; not an implementation claim.
frontierResolution.resolution: In d≠1 mod 4, the ring isomorphism carries norm -1 elements to units by Zsqrtd.norm_eq_one_iff, which uses absolute norm one. Surjectivity onto the norm sign -1 gives index two for its norm-one kernel. CA.4/negative-pell-classification supplies the least-negative-solution generator up to sign.

frontierResolution.disposition: Planning obligation supplied; not an implementation claim.
frontierResolution.resolution: Use O_K=Z[(1+θ)/2] and write units (a+bθ)/2 with equal parity and a²-db²=4ν, ν=±1. At d=1 mod 8 odd a,b are impossible, so the unit lies in Z[θ]. At d=5 mod 8 the cube has coefficients a(a²-3ν)/2 and b(a²-ν)/2, both integral, and norm ν. The cases d=5,13,17 and excluded d=1 are checked.

frontierResolution.resolution: The Minkowski bound is below five; primes over two and three generate. Dedekind–Kummer gives P₂²=(2); choose P₃ over three containing 2+θ, so (2+θ)=P₂P₃², checked by valuations and norm 18. No element has norm two, so P₂ is nonprincipal of order two. Thus P₃ has order four, the relation determinant is four and the cyclic group is complete.

frontierResolution.resolution: The bound is below seven; ramified P₂,P₃,P₅ generate. The relations 2e₂,2e₃,2e₅ and (1,1,1) come from (2),(3),(5),(θ), giving a quotient of order four. No element a+bθ has norm two, three or six: b≠0 has norm at least thirty. Hence the classes of P₂,P₃,P₂P₃ are three distinct nontrivial classes and the quotient is complete; Smith factors are 1,2,2.
